behavioral_notes.observation: Team membership is NOT a plain many2many: crm.team.member is an explicit join model carrying an `active` flag, so members can be archived without losing history. crm.team.member_ids is computed from crm_team_member_ids.user_id filtered on active memberships (_compute_member_ids depends on crm_team_member_ids.active); the inverse (_inverse_member_ids) creates missing crm.team.member rows for added users and (de)activates rows rather than deleting them. Multi vs mono membership is gated by the ir.config_parameter 'sales_team.membership_multi' (_compute_is_membership_multi); in mono mode a user may sit on only one active team and crm.team.member.create/write call _synchronize_memberships to auto-archive the user's competing memberships, while member_warning is computed to warn before that archive happens.

The team-assignment helper that the whole sales stack reuses to stamp team_id defaults on downstream documents (crm.lead, sale.order, account.move, pos.order...). It is deliberately NOT wired into default_get because it takes user_id + an optional domain (e.g. use_lead=True); other models' default_team methods call it. Resolution is a 5-step fallback honouring multi-company (valid_cids): (1) one of my teams as member OR leader matching the domain, (2) any of my teams, (3) the context default_team_id, (4) any company-visible team matching the domain, (5) any company-visible team. This single heuristic centralizes 'which sales team owns this record' across modules.

sales_team ships the Sales dashboard scaffolding that crm/sale fill in. The crm_team_view_kanban_dashboard kanban renders one card per team with a manage menu (View / New / Reporting) and a kanban_color_picker, and its card action is type='object' action_primary_channel_button — a SKELETON method returning False here, overridden downstream to open the team's pipeline. _compute_dashboard_button_name is likewise a placeholder ('Big Pretty Button :)') overloaded by crm/sale to label the action with live counts. Which teams appear on the dashboard is driven by favorite_user_ids: is_favorite ('Show on dashboard') has an inverse (_inverse_is_favorite, sudo) that adds/removes the current user, and creating a team or adding members auto-favourites them (_add_members_to_favorites). The progressbar/KPI numbers are not in this module; they are added by the consumers.

behavioral_notes.element: team_id scoping + record rules (crm_rule_all_salesteam, sale_team_comp_rule) + res.users.sale_team_id
behavioral_notes.observation: sales_team defines the security spine the sales docs inherit: three groups (group_sale_salesman 'Own Documents Only' -> group_sale_salesman_all_leads 'All Documents' -> group_sale_manager 'Administrator', chained via implied_ids) plus two ir.rule on crm.team — crm_rule_all_salesteam (the all-leads group sees every team) and sale_team_comp_rule (multi-company: company_id in company_ids + [False]). Downstream models (crm.lead, sale.order) add their OWN team_id/user_id-scoped record rules keyed to these same groups, so the salesman/all-leads/manager tier defined here governs visibility of every sales document. res.users.sale_team_id (_compute_sale_team_id) picks the user's main team as the OLDEST active membership (crm_team_member_ids sorted by create_date), and crm_team_ids is the set of active-membership teams; res.users.action_archive cascades to archive the user's memberships. company constraints (_constrains_company_members / _constrains_company_membership, _check_company_auto) keep a member's company aligned with the team's.

1 JS file, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components; 1 registry add (views:crm_team_form — the crm_team_form js_class on the team form view that drives the membership warning / multi-team activation UX). Asset bundles: web.assets_backend(1), web.assets_unit_tests(1). No OWL components, services or patches — the dashboard is plain kanban XML, not a custom OWL client action at this layer.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (sales force / sales organization administration)
classification.rationale: sales_team is a cross-cutting support/foundation module, not a value configuration of its own. It owns no document flow (0 routes, no state machine, no transform/solve/mediate loop) and produces no value stream — it defines the sales ORGANIZATION (crm.team, crm.team.member, the salesman/all-leads/manager group tier) and the reusable team_id-assignment heuristic + dashboard scaffolding that the real value modules consume: crm (shop) hangs its pipeline off crm.team, while sale and pos (chain) inherit its team_id scoping and security tiering for their order/invoice documents. By Stabell & Fjeldstad it is firm-infrastructure / support; its APQC home is 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services as the sales-force/sales-organization administration backbone rather than any specific 3.5.x selling activity, which live in the consuming modules.
classification.value_model_note: Defined as a reference/foundation consumed by crm, sale, pos — it has no value stream of its own (hence value_streams = []).
